           MOTION FOR EXTENSION OF COMPLIANCE DEADLINE OF THE
                   INDICATED PJM TRANSMISSION OWNERS
                    AND REQUEST FOR EXPEDITED ACTION
                     AND SHORTENED COMMENT PERIOD

        Pursuant to Rule 212 of the Rules of Practice and Procedure of the Federal Energy

Regulatory Commission’s (“Commission” or “FERC”),1 the Indicated PJM Transmission Owners

(“PJM Transmission Owners”)2 respectfully request that the Commission grant an extension of

time with respect to the compliance obligations imposed on the PJM Transmission Owners in the

        18 C.F.R. § 385.212 (2025).
2
          The Indicated PJM Transmission Owners are: American Electric Power Service Corporation on behalf of its
affiliates, Appalachian Power Company, Indiana Michigan Power Company, Kentucky Power Company, Kingsport
Power Company, Ohio Power Company, Wheeling Power Company, AEP Appalachian Transmission Company, Inc.,

Dominion Energy Virginia; Duke Energy Business Services, LLC for Duke Energy Kentucky, Inc. and Duke Energy
Ohio, Inc.; Duquesne Light Company; East Kentucky Power Cooperative, Inc.; Exelon Corporation on behalf of its
affiliates Atlantic City Electric Company, Baltimore Gas and Electric Company, Commonwealth Edison Company,
Commonwealth Edison Company of Indiana, Inc., Delmarva Power & Light Company, PECO Energy Company, and
Potomac Electric Power Company; FirstEnergy Service Company, on behalf of its affiliates American Transmission
Systems, Incorporated, Jersey Central Power & Light Company, Mid-Atlantic Interstate Transmission LLC, The
Potomac Edison Company, Monongahela Power Company, Keystone Appalachian Transmission Company, and
Trans-Allegheny Interstate Line Company (collectively, the “FirstEnergy Companies”); PPL Electric Utilities
Corporation; Public Service Electric and Gas Company; Rockland Electric Company; and the Southern Maryland
Electric Cooperative.
 Commission’s June 18, 2026 Order on Rehearing, Clarification, Compliance Filing, and Paper

Hearing in these proceedings.3 The PJM Transmission Owners request that the Commission

extend the compliance deadline in this proceeding for 90 days, until November 16, 2026,4 so that

it aligns with the deadline by which PJM and the PJM Transmission Owners have requested to

submit one or more filings pursuant to section 205 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”) in response

to the Commission’s show cause order in Docket No. EL26-67-000.5

        Good cause exists to grant this motion because the issues the Commission has required

PJM and the PJM Transmission Owners to address in the compliance filing in the above-captioned

proceedings significantly overlap those being addressed by PJM and the PJM Transmission

Owners in response to the PJM Show Cause Order.6 Granting this request will ensure the PJM

Transmission Owners have adequate time to determine the appropriate additions and revisions to

the PJM Open Access Transmission Tariff (“PJM Tariff” or “Tariff”) for transmission services

applicable to co-located load customers as well as other large load customers, and will avoid

unnecessary duplication, confusion, and potential inconsistencies between provisions being

developed to address issues relevant to both proceedings. The PJM Transmission Owners further

request a shortened comment period of five (5) days to facilitate the Commission’s issuance of an

order granting the motion to extend the compliance deadline no later than August 10, 2026.


3
        PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., et al., 195 FERC ¶ 61,209 (2026) (“June 18 Order”).
4
        November 16 is the first business day after the end of the 90-day abeyance period.
5
        See PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., et al., 195 FERC ¶ 61,211 (2026) (“PJM Show Cause Order”); see also
Motion for Abeyance of the Indicated PJM Transmission Owners and Request for Expedited Action and Shortened
Comment Period, Docket No. EL26-67-000 (filed July 28, 2026).
In the event that the Commission grants less than a 90-day abeyance in the PJM Show Cause Order proceeding, the
PJM Transmission Owners request the Commission adopt that date as the deadline for submitting the compliance
filing required in the instant proceedings.
6
          The PJM Transmission Owners understand that PJM will submit certain of the compliance changes directed
to it by the June 18 Order by the existing 60-day deadline of August 17, 2026. The PJM Transmission Owners are
currently working with PJM to determine if it would be necessary or efficient to submit certain of their own
complementary compliance changes by August 17, 2026 as well.


                                                        2
 I.       BACKGROUND

         A.       The PJM Co-Located Load Proceeding

         On December 18, 2025, the Commission issued an order in Docket Nos. EL25-49-000, et

al., pursuant to section 206 of the FPA, finding the PJM Tariff unjust and unreasonable because it

does not contain provisions addressing with sufficient clarity or consistency the rates, terms, and

conditions of service that apply to generators serving Co-Located Load and Eligible Customers

taking transmission service on behalf of Co-Located Load.7

         The Commission directed PJM, inter alia, to submit revisions to its Tariff to require that

the Eligible Customer taking transmission service on behalf of the Co-Located Load takes one of

three transmission services: (1) Network Integration Transmission Service (“NITS”), including a

new interim, non-firm transmission service available until all Network Upgrades necessary to

provide the requested NITS are complete (“Interim NITS”), (2) a new Firm Contract Demand

(“Firm Contract Demand”) transmission service, or (3) a new Non-Firm Contract Demand (“Non-

Firm Contract Demand”) transmission service.8 The Commission also established a paper hearing

to determine the just and reasonable rates, terms, and conditions for these new transmission

services.9 On February 23, 2026, in Docket Nos. EL25-49-000, et al., PJM and the PJM

Transmission Owners each submitted an initial brief to address the Commission’s paper hearing

questions with respect to the new transmission services. On March 25, 2026, and on April 24,

2026, various parties submitted response briefs and reply briefs, respectively.




7
         PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 193 FERC ¶ 61,217, at P 2 (2025) (“December Order”).
8
         December Order at P 2.
9
         Id. at PP 2, 194, 219. The Commission also found the Behind the Meter Generation (“BTMG”) rules in the
Tariff to be no longer just and reasonable, and the Commission directed PJM to submit in its compliance filing
revisions to its Tariff to revise the retail BTMG netting rules and to implement a transition process for existing BTMG
participants. Id. at PP 2, 179, 186, 221-224.



                                                          3
        In the June 18 Order, the Commission addressed the rates, terms, and conditions for the

required new transmission services as developed through the paper hearing submissions, including

the rate proposals made by the PJM Transmission Owners. The Commission accepted certain of

the proposals and rejected others, and directed PJM and the PJM Transmission Owners to submit

compliance filings with 60 days of the date of the June 18 Order (i.e., August 17, 2026) to reflect

the rates, terms, and conditions for the new transmission services in the PJM Tariff.10

       B.       The PJM Large Load Show Cause Proceeding

       On June 18, 2026, the Commission also issued a show cause order under section 206 of the

FPA to PJM, together with the PJM Transmission Owners, directing PJM to justify or reform the

Tariff provisions governing how large loads connect to and receive service from the transmission

system.11 The PJM Show Cause Order preliminarily found that PJM’s Tariff appeared to be unjust,

unreasonable, or unduly discriminatory or preferential because of a lack of sufficiently clear and

consistent provisions to address service for large loads and related configurations.12         The

Commission therefore directed PJM and the PJM Transmission Owners, within 60 days, to show

cause why the Tariff remains just and reasonable without provisions addressing:             (1) the

application process, study procedures, and ongoing operational requirements for Eligible

Customers seeking transmission service on behalf of large loads; (2) additional transparency

concerning Network Upgrade costs for such service, together with the absence of a pro forma cost

recovery agreement and a mechanism to ensure related payments are properly credited to

transmission owners’ revenue requirements; (3) transmission service options tailored to flexible

large loads willing and able to limit their use of the transmission system under certain conditions;


10
       June 18 Order at Ordering Para. (C)-(H).
11
       PJM Show Cause Order at PP 3, 35.
12
       Id. at PP 3, 35.



                                                  4
 and (4) rates, terms, and conditions applicable to interconnection customers serving “electrically

proximate large load” or co-located load.13 The Commission directed PJM either to justify the

absence of such provisions or to propose Tariff revisions addressing those concerns.14

        The PJM Show Cause Order indicated that the Commission would consider requests from

PJM and/or transmission owners to hold all or certain aspects of the FPA section 206 proceeding

in abeyance, for up to 90 days, including the August 17, 2026, deadline to respond.15 The

Commission explained that the purpose of such an abeyance would be to provide PJM and the

PJM Transmission Owners time while they work through the stakeholder process to develop FPA

section 205 filings to revise the PJM Tariff to address the issues raised in the PJM Show Cause

Order.16

II.     MOTION FOR EXTENSION

        On the same date as the instant motion, the PJM Transmission Owners are submitting a

motion, consistent with the PJM Show Cause Order, requesting that the Commission hold the

deadline to respond to that order in abeyance for a 90-day period in order to allow the PJM

Transmission Owners to address, through one or more FPA section 205 filings, the issues

identified in the PJM Show Cause Order. The PJM Transmission Owners understand that PJM is

submitting a substantially similar request. In their abeyance motion, the PJM Transmission

Owners commit to file their FPA section 205 filing(s) responsive to the PJM Show Cause Order




13
        Id.
14
        Id.
15
         Id. at P 39. Because 60 days from issuance of the PJM Show Cause Order falls on a Saturday, the deadline
to respond does not end until the close of business on Monday, August 17. See 18 C.F.R. § 385.2007(a)(2).
16
        PJM Show Cause Order at P 39.



                                                       5
 by no later than November 16, 2026, which is the date 90 days after the deadline to respond to the

PJM Show Cause Order.17

        The issues the PJM Transmission Owners are addressing in response to the PJM Show

Cause Order substantially overlap with those that the Commission directed the PJM Transmission

Owners to address in the June 18 Order. Many of the issues addressed in the PJM Show Cause

Order incorporate or otherwise build off of the requirements imposed by the Commission in the

PJM Co-Located Load proceeding. For instance, the PJM Show Cause Order preliminarily found

that new transmission services should be available to “flexible large loads” willing and able to

limit their withdrawals, specifically the three new services it required in the PJM Co-Located Load

proceeding: (1) Interim NITS, (2) Firm Contract Demand, and (3) Non-Firm Contract Demand.18

In effect, the PJM Show Cause Order contemplates expanding the scope of these new transmission

services to a broader set of customers. Therefore, the PJM Transmission Owners anticipate that

the underlying rate design approaches that the Commission directed be adopted in compliance with

the June 18 Order would serve as the basis for these new services as applied to both Co-Located

Load customers and flexible large load customers. However, the PJM Transmission Owners will

still need to carefully consider, in coordination with PJM and other interested stakeholders, what

additions and modifications are necessary to adapt those rate proposals to new services available

under the PJM Show Cause Order.

        Given the substantial overlap between the requirements in the two orders, the best approach

is for PJM and the PJM Transmission Owners to develop the Co-Located Load compliance filing




17
          See id. (“The Commission will consider requests from PJM and/or the Transmission Owners to hold, for up
to 90 days, all or certain aspects of this FPA section 206 proceeding in abeyance, including the deadline to respond
to this order.”) (emphasis added).
18
        Id. at 86.



                                                         6
 and the FPA section 205 filing(s) holistically, rather than separately, and to file them on the same

date. This approach has several benefits. First, it will be more efficient for PJM, the PJM

Transmission Owners, and PJM stakeholders to prepare and consider the necessary tariff changes

together. Absent this coordination, PJM and the PJM Transmission Owners will inevitably end

up significantly duplicating their design and stakeholder outreach efforts. A holistic process will

also avoid potential confusion on the part of PJM stakeholders regarding the scope and impact of

proposed procedures and other rates, terms, and conditions that will likely end up affecting both

Co-Located Loads and other large load customers. An approach whereby PJM and the PJM

Stakeholders are required to submit a compliance filing in the Co-Located Load proceeding at an

earlier time most likely would result in the need to amend Tariff revisions submitted in the Co-

Located Load compliance filing in response to the PJM Show Cause Order, thus creating the risk

of inconsistencies between overlapping and superseding tariff versions. Finally, having a single

filing date for both proceedings will allow interested parties to address any issues or concerns with

the proposed tariff provisions filed by PJM and the PJM Transmission Owners, and will allow the

Commission to review those revisions, in a coherent and administratively efficient fashion.

       A modest 90-day extension of the compliance directives in the June 18 Order will not

unfairly prejudice PJM stakeholders or other interested parties. As discussed above, addressing

the Co-Located Load revisions in conjunction with the issues identified in the PJM Show Cause

Order will provide several advantages to interested parties. Moreover, this extension will not

impact the ultimate effective date of any of the proposed revisions relating to the June 18 Order or

the PJM Show Cause Order. For these reasons, the PJM Transmission Owners respectfully request

that the Commission grant a 90-day extension so that the deadline for submitting the compliance




                                                 7
 filing in response to the June 18 Order will be the same as the deadline for FPA section 205 filing(s)

made in response to the PJM Show Cause Order: November 16, 2026.

III.   REQUEST FOR EXPEDITED CONSIDERATION AND SHORTENED
       COMMENT PERIOD

       The PJM Transmission Owners request expedited consideration of this motion for

extension and request that the Commission issue an order granting the motion no later than August

10, 2026. Expedited consideration and the issuance of an order by that date will provide the PJM

Transmission Owners sufficient assurance that they will have adequate time to develop and submit

both the June 18 Order compliance filing, as well as one or more FPA section 205 filings necessary

to implement the PJM Show Cause Order. Expedited consideration will also allow the PJM

Transmission Owners to focus their efforts on developing these filings in a holistic consistent

fashion, rather than spending critical time preparing a separate Co-Located Load compliance filing

that likely would require substantial subsequent amendments. Consistent with this request, the

PJM Transmission Owners also seek a shortened comment period on this motion for an extension

of time. Specifically, the PJM Transmission Owners request that the Commission establish a

comment period of five (5) days. Good cause exists to grant a shortened comment period for the

reasons set forth above. Moreover, no party will be prejudiced as a result of granting a five (5)

day comment period, as the additional time and certainty afforded by an expedited order will

accrue to the benefit of stakeholders by providing the PJM Transmission Owners sufficient time

to solicit and consider stakeholder feedback on their proposals.




                                                  8
 IV.    CONCLUSION

       For the reasons set forth above, the PJM Transmission Owners’ request that the

Commission establish a five (5) day comment period for answers to this motion, and issue an order

on or before August 10, 2026, granting the PJM Transmission Owners’ request to extend the

compliance deadline in the above-captioned proceedings until November 16, 2026, or whatever

alternative date the Commission adopts as the deadline to submit one or more FPA section 205

filings in response to the PJM Show Cause Order.
